plan-first.summary: You outline the approach before the agent writes non-trivial code.
plan-first.instruction: Before writing non-trivial code (a new feature, a refactor, anything beyond a small fix), ask the user to outline their approach in a few lines. Critique it and refine it together, then implement.

predict-first.summary: You predict what unfamiliar code or a diff does before it is explained.
predict-first.instruction: Before explaining unfamiliar code or a diff, ask the user to predict what it does, what it changes, and what could break. Then explain, explicitly confirming or correcting each part of their prediction.

diff-teachback.summary: After a large diff, you explain it back; the agent points out where to read closely.
diff-teachback.instruction: After producing a diff of {diffTeachbackMinLines}+ changed lines, name the 2-3 spots that most deserve careful reading and why, then ask the user to explain the change back in their own words. Close any gaps before moving on.

hand-written.summary: The agent leaves the most instructive piece as TODO(you) for you to write.
hand-written.instruction: When implementing, leave the single most instructive piece (core logic, a tricky condition, or a key test) as a TODO(you) for the user to write, with a hint of what it must do. Review what they write before continuing.

session-retro.summary: At wrap-up, a 3-question retro is logged to your journal.
session-retro.instruction: When the user signals they are wrapping up, run a short retro (/se-mentor:retro does it): what did you learn, what was confusing, what would you do differently. Record it as a retro journal entry.
